question: If S-104's next RM-221 shipment ships two weeks late, when will DC-EAST run out of Lacrivia, when will supply recover there, and which customers get supply first under our allocation rules?
answer:
DC-EAST has probably already run out of Lacrivia, around 26–27 Sep 2026. If S-104's next RM-221 shipment ships two weeks late, supply at DC-EAST comes back on about 10 Dec 2026, a gap of roughly 75 days. Under our allocation rule, three Tier A health systems get supply first, then two Tier B systems, then everyone else in proportion to their prescriptions.

**1. When DC-EAST runs out.** The stockout is already happening; the late shipment only makes it last longer.

| Pack | On hand (25 Sep) | Safety stock | Shipped per day (last 28 days) | Days of supply | Stock-out date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL | 46 | 471 | 36.7 | 1.3 | about 26 Sep |
| Lacrivia 10 mL | 34 | 233 | 15.1 | 2.3 | about 27 Sep |

**2. When supply recovers.**
- **The shipment:** the next S-104 order for RM-221 is PO005791 (4,200 units), promised to ship 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships 21 Oct.
- **Lead time:** it takes 50 days from S-104 shipping to finished Lacrivia reaching DC-EAST:
  - 6 days transit to the premix supplier
  - 10 days to make, test and ship the premix (CMP-310)
  - 12 days for the two emulsion stages
  - 3 days to fill the bottles
  - 19 days for final release, including the 14-day sterility test and 4 days to the DC
- **Recovery date:** 21 Oct + 50 days = **10 Dec 2026**. If the shipment were on time, recovery would be 26 Nov, so the delay adds 14 days.
- **Size of the gap:** about 75 days. At current rates that is roughly 2,750 units of 5 mL and 1,120 units of 10 mL that DC-EAST can't supply.
- **Partial cover from other DCs:** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST together hold 695 units of 5 mL and 391 of 10 mL above their safety stock. That covers about 19 and 26 days of DC-EAST demand, not the whole gap. Moving stock between DCs needs Supply Planning approval.

**3. Who gets supply first (rule BR-ALLOC-01).** Prescription counts (TRx) are for Lacrivia, last 13 weeks, from clinics in DC-EAST states only.

1. **Tier A contracts:**
   - Riverbend Health System (AC00059): 836
   - Oak Hollow Health System (AC00038): 708
   - Northfield Health System (AC00117): 533
2. **Tier B contracts:**
   - Clearview Health System (AC00001): 530. Its contract runs to 31 Dec, which is after recovery.
   - Sunridge Health System (AC00138): 428
3. **Everyone else, in proportion to their 2,135 TRx.** The largest shares are:
   - Brightwater Health System: 19.4%
   - Stonegate Health System: 15.0%
   - Sunridge Vision Associates 20: 9.3%
   - Willow Creek Health System: 8.8%
   - Harbor Point Vision Associates 2: 6.5%
   - Highland Vision Associates 26: 6.2%
   - 12 smaller accounts share the remaining 34.8%.

The two contract tiers account for 3,035 of the 5,170 DC-EAST prescriptions (59%). Sunridge Vision Associates 20 and the other "Vision Associates" clinics are independent top-level accounts. They don't take the contract tier of the similarly named health systems.

**Sources and definitions:**
- **Knowledge layer:** the supply trace for S-104 and RM-221 showed RM-221 is single-source (the backup supplier S-131 isn't qualified). It feeds both Lacrivia packs, cyclosporine 5 mL and 11 lens-care products.
- **Business rules:**
  - BR-LEAD-01 and the standard stage times give the 50-day lead time.
  - BR-ALLOC-01 sets the allocation order.
  - BR-CUST-01 means clinics are rolled up to their top-level account.
  - BR-REGION-01 serves each account from its state's DC. DC-EAST covers NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC and OH.
- **Reference data:** the supply contract tiers come from the contract system.
- **Tables (all approved sources):**
  - Supply warehouse: purchase orders, DC inventory and wholesaler shipments.
  - Commercial warehouse: weekly prescriptions, prescribers and accounts, joined using the approved path.
- **Access check:** the policy check allowed access for your role with no masking.

**Assumptions:**
- Demand is based on wholesaler shipments over the last 28 days. The last 13 weeks means the 13 most recent weeks of prescription data.
- Standard lead times are used, with no expediting and no plant capacity limits.
- I assumed the delayed order is the lot that restocks DC-EAST. Earlier RM-221 lots shipped 9–24 Sep are already in production and could arrive around late Oct to mid-Nov at standard times. RM-221 is shared with 13 other products, though, so I didn't count those lots toward Lacrivia at DC-EAST. Confirming how that material is assigned could bring partial recovery forward.

I've logged this analysis as trace 3731d061.

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND MATERIAL_ID='RM-221' AND (STATUS <> 'CLOSED' OR PROMISED_SHIP_DT >= '2026-08-01') ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT, ON_HAND_UNITS, SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SNAPSHOT_DT >= '2026-08-01' ORDER BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT

SELECT MATERIAL_ID, DATEADD(day, -((DATEDIFF(day,'2026-01-02',SHIP_DT)) % 7), SHIP_DT) AS WK, SUM(UNITS) AS UNITS, COUNT(*) AS N FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SHIP_DT >= '2026-07-01' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID, DATEADD(day, -((DATEDIFF(day,'2026-01-02',SHIP_DT)) % 7), SHIP_DT) ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, WK

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, MAX(SHIP_DT) AS LAST_SHIP, SUM(CASE WHEN SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,'2026-09-30') THEN UNITS ELSE 0 END) AS U28_TO_0930, SUM(CASE WHEN SHIP_DT > '2026-08-28' AND SHIP_DT <= '2026-09-25' THEN UNITS ELSE 0 END) AS U28_TO_0925 FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID

WITH RECURSIVE anc AS (
  SELECT ACCOUNT_ID, ACCOUNT_ID AS TOP_ID, PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID, 0 AS LVL FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT
  UNION ALL
  SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, p.ACCOUNT_ID, p.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID, a.LVL+1 FROM anc a JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p ON a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID = p.ACCOUNT_ID WHERE a.LVL < 10
), top AS (SELECT ACCOUNT_ID, TOP_ID FROM anc WHERE PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID IS NULL),
wks AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (
  SELECT t.TOP_ID, r.PROD_NDC11, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) TRX
  FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r
  JOIN wks w ON r.WK_END_DT = w.WK_END_DT
  JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr ON r.PRSCRBR_ME = pr.PRSCRBR_ME
  JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a ON pr.ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
  JOIN top t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
  WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') AND a.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH')
  GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT rx.TOP_ID, ta.ACCOUNT_NM, ta.ACCT_TYP, ta.STATE,
  SUM(CASE WHEN PROD_NDC11='99101010105' THEN TRX ELSE 0 END) TRX_5ML,
  SUM(CASE WHEN PROD_NDC11='99101010110' THEN TRX ELSE 0 END) TRX_10ML,
  SUM(TRX) TRX_TOTAL,
  ROUND(100*SUM(TRX)/SUM(SUM(TRX)) OVER (),2) PCT
FROM rx JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT ta ON ta.ACCOUNT_ID = rx.TOP_ID
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY TRX_TOTAL DESC
